headline: High: Goose’s filesystem/MCP write access can conflict with Authelia’s broad network/OAuth role, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and compliance risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP servers, so it may ingest Authelia-produced files or outputs as trusted content. Authelia exposes OAuth/OIDC and ForwardAuth interfaces, but no direct shared channel is documented. The interaction is plausible in default setups via files or extensions, so I choose medium rather than low because the bridge is broader than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Goose is configured to read Authelia-generated files or MCP outputs as instructions, injection is possible.
IF Authelia outputs are copied into Goose-managed workspaces without provenance checks, malicious content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Authelia outputs into Goose prompts.
Add a provenance prefix to Authelia-generated artifacts.
Restrict Goose MCP servers to allowlisted, read-only endpoints.
Use separate directories for Authelia configs and Goose workspaces.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches files in the cwd and user filesystem and has broad network egress; Authelia also has broad network egress and handles OAuth/OIDC flows. Even though Authelia’s touched data classes are empty, Goose can expose local files or secrets from the workspace if they are present. The shared filesystem path makes leakage plausible in default use, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Goose’s workspace, Goose can read them and transmit them over network egress.
IF Authelia is configured with secrets or identity metadata in shared files, Goose may access them through the filesystem.
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of Goose’s workspace.
Run Goose in a dedicated directory with minimal contents.
Rotate any secrets stored in shared files.
Restrict Goose network egress to approved destinations.
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem and egress sandboxing per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem; Authelia has broad network egress and acts as an auth service. If both operate on the same repo or config tree, Goose can overwrite files while Authelia serves or consumes them, creating default write conflicts and potentially irreversible repo state changes. Uncertainty about exact shared paths pushes this to high.
conditions: IF Authelia config or policy files live in the same directory Goose edits, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Goose runs multiple instances against the same filesystem, git state can diverge or be corrupted.
mitigations: Separate Authelia config repos from Goose workspaces.
Pause Goose before editing shared git state.
Use branch-per-task for Goose changes.
Lock shared directories during Authelia updates.
requires-engineering: add file-locking and transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on files and MCP outputs, so if it consumes Authelia-generated configuration or policy text without verification, downstream mistakes can cascade into incorrect auth behavior. Authelia itself is an auth component, but no direct evidence shows it validates Goose’s outputs. The pathway exists in default workflows where Goose edits files that Authelia later uses, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Goose writes Authelia config or policy files that are later deployed, errors can propagate downstream.
IF Authelia consumes Goose-authored artifacts without review, incorrect settings can affect authentication flows.
mitigations: Require human review before deploying Goose-authored auth changes.
Validate Authelia configs with a dry run.
Keep Goose outputs in a staging directory.
Add schema checks for auth policy files.
requires-engineering: wire automated verification gates into deployment.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service with broad network egress, while Goose handles local files and provider keys. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for either agent, and Authelia’s touched data classes are empty. The main compliance concern is operational: if regulated identity data is placed in Goose’s workspace, it could be exposed, but that requires an unusual setup, so low fits.
conditions: IF regulated identity data is stored in Goose’s workspace, compliance controls may be bypassed.
IF Authelia is used with jurisdiction-specific identity data and Goose has access to the same files, retention and access policies may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated identity data out of Goose workspaces.
Document which files Authelia may read or write.
Limit Goose access to non-regulated projects.
Review retention settings for shared directories.
requires-engineering: implement data-class-based access controls.
